observation_summary: The MonthDay class fails when performing arithmetic operations (plus/minus months/days) on leap day (February 29th). It throws an IllegalFieldValueException because it attempts to validate the day-of-month against a non-leap year range (1-28) during the intermediate calculation steps, or it incorrectly adjusts the date to February 28th.
hypothesis: The algorithm for adding/subtracting months or days to a MonthDay object does not correctly handle the leap day (February 29th) because it performs intermediate calculations using a default or non-leap year chronology, causing the validation logic in FieldUtils.verifyValueBounds to trigger an exception or force an incorrect adjustment.
prediction: The fix will involve modifying the add/subtract logic in MonthDay or the underlying Chronology to handle leap day arithmetic by either deferring validation until the final result is computed or by using a chronology that supports leap years during the intermediate steps.
experiment_rationale: The stack trace shows the failure occurs inside FieldUtils.verifyValueBounds, which is called by PreciseDurationDateTimeField.set during the addition process. This confirms that the logic is attempting to set a day-of-month value (29) that is considered invalid in the current context, indicating an algorithmic flaw in how the date arithmetic is performed for partial dates.
reasoning_summary: The issue is an algorithmic failure in handling date arithmetic for partial dates (MonthDay) specifically on leap days. It is not a missing check (the check is working as intended for non-leap years), nor is it a simple assignment error. The procedure for adding/subtracting time units needs to be updated to correctly account for leap years, which is a classic Algorithm/Method defect.
evidence_used: org.joda.time.IllegalFieldValueException: Value 29 for dayOfMonth must be in the range [1,28]

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the error is thrown by a check, the check itself is correct for the context it is being applied in. The root cause is that the algorithm is applying the check in an invalid context (a non-leap year) for a leap day date.
